article:
Kevin Durant , over the course of his career, has earned $598.2 million, including the two- year ($90 million) deal he signed last season with the Houston Rockets , based on current and future salaries, according to ESPN's Sham Charania .
Durant surpassed LeBron James ($583.9 million) for the most career earnings in NBA history. And he will most likely earn over $600 million by the time he calls it a career.
Durant, along with his business partner Rich Klieman, has also made savvy investments off the court that have netted him some massive returns, including his latest investment into Hugging Face, an AI tools company.
Now, according to reports, the artificial intelligence tech giant Nvidia is slated to buy Hugging Face for $12.9 billion. If so, Durant stands to make $60 million, which is more money than he will make this season with the Rockets, according to Huddle Up Founder Joe Pompliano .
More NBA:
According to CNBC's April Roach and Kai Nicol-Schwarz ," A source familiar with the matter told CNBC they could "confirm acquisition [by Nvidia] has been part of ongoing and recent talks."
They spoke anonymously because the deal hasn't yet been announced.
During a recent appearance on CNBC's "Squawk Box Europe" Siddy Jobe , who is a fund manager at Eonopolis Exponential Technologies funds, shared that it made business sense for Nvidia to acquire Hugging Face.
"I think Nvidia is very much a community, a platform-based company, and in that respect, I think Hugging Face fits perfectly within that. There is this five-layer cake from Nvidia, and foundational models are one of them," Jobe said.
"It is clear that Nvidia wants to be integrated in the entire stack vertically, going from energy to foundational models and also to applications," he added.
Earlier this week, Hugging Face CEO Clément Delangue made his own appearance on CNBC's " Squawk on the Street ," sharing that China is winning the artificial intelligence race and could catch up with USA makers as early as next year.
"They're clearly dominating on open models right now, and I wouldn't be surprised if they start dominating at the frontier either by the end of this year or next year at the rate of progress," he said.
Over the years, Kevin Durant has invested in a variety of different companies, such as Whoop, Coinbase, Postmates, Acorns, Boardroom, Mercury, Rubrik, Overtime, Robinhood, and Postmates, to name a few.
An X account called Michael Burry Stock Tracker, which tracks the activity of the hedge fund manager highlighted in the movie "The Big Short," broke down Durant's initial investment and what they made after being sold.
• Hugging Face : $250K → $60M (+23,900%) • Whoop : $125M→ $10.1B (+7,980%) • Coinbase : $1.6B → $86B (+5,275%) • Mercury : $100M → $5.2B (+5,100%) • Robinhood : $5.6B → $99.4B (+1,675%) • Overtime : $31M → $800M (+2,480%) • Rubrik : $1.3B → $20.7B (+1,492%) • Postmates : $1M → $15M (+1,400%).
Durant also has invested into sports leagues and team franchises such as, Athletes Unlimited, Brooklyn Aces, NJ/NY Gotham FC, Philadelphia Union, and Paris Saint-Germain (PSG).
This story was originally published by Lindys Sports on Aug 29, 2026, where it first appeared in the NBA section. Add Lindys Sports as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
